QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_59

question.text: Under SAS-1100 a common DOUBLE-COUNTING risk is:

answer.text: Counting CSR-donor funds and ZCZP-bond funds for the same unit as two separate sources of impact

explanation.text: The Logic: A housing unit funded partly by CSR and partly by ZCZP may be claimed by both the CSR-Report and the SSE Annual Impact Report — resulting in inflated aggregate impact. SAS-1100 requires the SIA to de-duplicate funding-source attribution. The Trap: Options B, C, D are irrelevant. Cross-Exam Context: Double-counting logic across SAS standards and BRSR in III-A / III-C Compliance. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Ask the SE to provide a 'single-source' funding table — one unit, one dominant funder. Any unit funded >20% by multiple sources warrants proportional attribution disclosure.
